attacks.challenge: surrogate trace may hide real DP6 structure
attacks.evidence: frozen HLS semantics replayed and canonical nonce-1200 mh/transcript/final vector matched exactly

attacks.challenge: 16 adjacent nonces may accidentally look uniform
attacks.evidence: second 16-trace corpus varies hdr/task/prev/height/nonce deterministically and reproduces the bank/locality result

attacks.challenge: chosen bank functions may hide an exploitable mapping
attacks.evidence: 408 linear/xor interleave functions over 32/64/128/256-byte granularities and 16..256 banks; train selection followed by disjoint holdout evaluation

attacks.challenge: optional RW5 memory opcodes show non-uniform bank occupancy
attacks.evidence: opcode-specific skew exists, but combined mandatory+extra traces remain near-balanced and fixed-64-bank mapping-sensitive hottest-bank load headroom is about 0.45% canonical and 0.12% diverse holdout

attacks.challenge: global occupancy may hide exploitable short-lag locality
attacks.evidence: B64 bank-collision ratios for lags 1..1024 stay within about 0.35% of random baseline; row-hit and same-page probabilities remain extremely small

attacks.challenge: multiple nonces may collide in the same bank predictably
attacks.evidence: same-step cross-nonce B64 collision ratio is 0.99927x random on canonical corpus and 0.99910x on diverse corpus

attacks.challenge: a real HBM/DRAM/custom controller may use a mapping outside the modeled family
attacks.evidence: requires concrete controller mapping/timing or physical specialized evidence; cannot be promoted to a generic DP6 weakness without such evidence
